newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southwest prices firm on nuke refuel, NW flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southwest prices firm on nuke refuel, NW flat.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Southwest continued to firm as an Arizona nuclear unit prepared to shut down for planned refueling, while Northwest prices were mostly flat, market sources said Friday.
"People expected prices to soften with all the warm weather and the weekend coming, but buyers were in at the open and the bids kept rising," said one trader.
Sources said next-day Palo Verde prices traded early at $13.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), but rose as high as $14.50.
The 1,221 MW unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant near Wintersburg, Ariz., was expected to be completely off-line by midnight Friday for a 50-day refueling outage.
In addition, restart of the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California was delayed to early March after the discovery of a generator tube leak earlier this week.
The unit was shut Nov 30 for a scheduled refueling outage, which had already been extended to the end of February so that tube repairs could be carried out.

In the Northwest the 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear unit in Washington was running at 55 percent of capacity at the request of Bonneville Power Administration, which has excess supplies of low-cost hydropower.

Northwest temperatures were expected to be be five to 10 degrees F above normal Saturday through Tuesday, while temperatures in the Southwest were forecasts at six to 12 degrees above normal through early next week.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Monday was quoted at $9.25-10.25 a megawatt hour (MWh), little changed from $9.50-10.50 for Friday.
Firm, off-peak COB quotes for Monday were at $6.00-7.00.
Firm, peak electricity at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) for Monday was unchanged at $8.50-9.50.
Off-peak Mid-C for day-ahead delivery was quoted at $5.50-6.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was quoted at $13.50-14.50, compared with $13.00-14.00 for Friday.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $13.00-14.00, while off-peak was at $7.50-8.00.
